5	//! exist inside a running agent session. So Vajra's job for a named role is two things, both in this
6	//! module's contract:
7	//!   1. **Scaffold** the role as a native subagent definition (`.claude/agents/<name>.md`), rendered
8	//!      from ONE canonical source (the S104/S99 no-drift rule) — the same way `vajra init` already

11	//!   2. **Govern the handoff.** The subagent returns a findings brief; Vajra wraps it into a
12	//!      delta-tracked handoff in the `.ai/` spine (the memory — no new store) and FAIL-CLOSES on an
13	//!      unknown role, missing/empty findings, or a handoff that would not validate.
14	//!

16	//! delta, one hash). The impure edges (reading findings, writing files, git) live in `cli::next` /
17	//! `cli::init`. Everything here is unit-testable without spawning anything.

78	    /// The `--role <name>` key and the subagent `name:`. Lower-case, stable — the join key.
79	    pub name: &'static str,
80	    /// One line describing WHEN to use this role — the subagent frontmatter `description:`.
81	    pub description: &'static str,
82	    /// The role-scoping system prompt — the subagent definition body.
83	    pub system_prompt: &'static str,
84	    /// This role's tool grant, rendered verbatim into the subagent frontmatter `tools:`. Per-role
85	    /// (S114) — it was hardcoded to the Researcher's list while only one role existed, which would
86	    /// have silently handed every future role the Researcher's web access.
87	    ///

89	    /// granted `Bash, Write, Edit` because QA evidence that was never run is not evidence. That is
90	    /// the materially bigger governance decision the S114 note said none had taken — it is taken

92	    pub tools: &'static str,

109	const RESEARCHER_SYSTEM_PROMPT: &str = "You are the Researcher on a governed software team. \

111	findings brief.\n\
112	Rules:\n\
113	- Do NOT write, edit, or run code. You investigate and report only.\n\
114	- Lead with the answer, then the few facts that support it.\n\
115	- Prefer specifics (names, numbers, versions, trade-offs) over generalities.\n\
116	- If the question is ambiguous or you are unsure, say so plainly — never invent facts or sources.\n\

119	/// The Reviewer's contract (S114). This is the brief this repo has re-typed from memory every
120	/// session for 47 cold reviews — made canonical here, which is the whole point of `ROLES`.

123	/// the verdict it returns is a **pre-stage input**, and the canonical, gated record of the verdict
124	/// stays `sessions/session-NN-review.md` — this agent never writes that file (it has no write tool

127	    "You are the Fidelity Reviewer on a governed software \
128	team. Your ONE job is an INDEPENDENT, ADVERSARIAL cold review of a delivery you did not build.\n\

130	Judge from those. Do not accept the builder's own summary as evidence.\n\
131	Rules:\n\
132	- Do NOT write, edit, or run code. You read and judge only.\n\
133	- Grade EVERY numbered requirement in the prompt: SHIPPED / PARTIAL / NOT-BUILT, each with the \
134	concrete evidence in the diff that earns the grade. A requirement with no evidence is NOT-BUILT.\n\
135	- Following the rules is not delivering what was asked: a green verify script proves discipline, \
136	never fidelity. Never grade from test counts alone.\n\
137	- Name THE FAKEST GREEN — the thing that looks done but is hollow (a check that would pass if the \
138	feature were deleted, a marker the author simply typed, an assertion that cannot fail).\n\
139	- Never self-certify and never soften: if the delivery is short, say so.\n\
140	Shape your brief so it can be landed without rewriting — the closeout gate reads the landed record \
141	and FAILS unless it carries all three of these:\n\
142	- a per-requirement MARKDOWN TABLE — the gate counts verdict words only on `|`-delimited rows and \
143	requires at least three of them, so one row per requirement carrying SHIPPED / PARTIAL / NOT-BUILT \
144	(a bulleted list with the same words does NOT pass),\n\
145	- a canonical `**Verdict:** ACCEPT` or `**Verdict:** REJECT` line (the word buried in a heading \
146	does not count),\n\
147	- a count of the form `X of N SHIPPED`.\n\
148	The full contract you are performing is `reviewer/SKILL.md` in this repo — READ IT before you \
149	judge; it is canonical and this brief is its dispatch-time summary, never a competing version.\n\
150	Your verdict is a PRE-STAGE INPUT. The canonical, gated record of the fidelity verdict is \
151	`sessions/session-NN-review.md` (read by `verify-closeout.sh`, attested by a `**Review-Inputs-SHA:**` \
152	the orchestrator computes, chained in the ledger) — you do not write it, and you are not its \
153	replacement.";

183	/// The QA Specialist's contract (S121). The fleet's first role granted execution: it runs the
184	/// session's verify script and reports what actually ran. Its value so far is measured as
185	/// INDEPENDENCE, not execution — see the module header; the executor thesis is unproven. The classification it is asked for is the S120 GT finding

187	/// feature being deleted), while a grep asserting ARCHITECTURE (one source of truth, no collision)
188	/// is structural and legitimate. It reports; it never edits the product under test.
189	const QA_SPECIALIST_SYSTEM_PROMPT: &str = "You are the QA Specialist on a governed software team. \
190	Your ONE job is to RUN the session's verification and report what actually executed.\n\
191	You are the first role on this team that can execute — you have Bash — because QA evidence that \
192	was never run is not evidence. Use that grant to RUN and to RECORD, never to change the thing you \
193	are testing.\n\
194	You will be pointed at a disposable clean-room checkout, not the source repo (S123 — \
195	`vajra next --role qa-specialist --clean-room-open`). Run every command inside that path. This is \

198	- RUN the session's `scripts/verify-session-NN.sh` for the session number you are given. Report its \

201	  - EXECUTE-BASED — it runs the product (the binary, `cargo test`, a script) and asserts on real \

203	  - BEHAVIORAL SOURCE GREP — it greps source for a message, flag, or prompt string and treats \
204	finding that string as proof the feature works. This is HOLLOW: it would still pass if the feature \

206	  A grep that asserts ARCHITECTURE instead of behaviour (one source of truth, no second copy, no \
207	name collision, a file's absence) is STRUCTURAL, not hollow — name it as such and keep it out of \

209	- REPORT, every time: how many checks fall in each class, the NAME of every hollow check, and the \
210	live output that proves you ran the suite (the exit code and the summary lines).\n\

212	Fixing what you just tested destroys the independence that makes your report worth reading.\n\
213	- If the verify script is missing, or will not run, SAY SO and STOP. A QA pass you could not run is \

215	- A green suite is not a passing delivery: say plainly what the suite never exercised.\n\
216	Your output is an evidence brief, not a verdict on the delivery — grading the requirements is the \
217	Fidelity Reviewer's job, and the gated record of that verdict is `sessions/session-NN-review.md`, \

231	Rules:\n\
232	- Do NOT write, edit, or run code, and do NOT write the prompt file yourself — you propose, the \
233	author records. You have no Write or Edit tool, by design.\n\
234	- Propose text for all four sections the gate requires by name: Goal, Deliverables, Acceptance, \
235	Guardrails. A prompt missing any of them is ill-formed and BLOCKS the advance into that session.\n\
236	- Write acceptance criteria as numbered, testable EARS-style lines — WHEN <x> THEN <observable \

238	the author can say whether it passed.\n\
239	- Propose a `## Delta` block whose bullets each carry an OpenSpec marker — `+` added, `~` \

248	- If the intent is ambiguous enough that two readings would produce different sessions, say so \

665	/// section, minus heading lines. `None` when the frontmatter fence or the delta section is absent.
666	/// Public so the ingest can extract a PRIOR handoff's body to feed `compute_delta` on a re-run.
667	pub fn handoff_body(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
668	    let after_fm = text.strip_prefix("---\n")?;
669	    let close = after_fm.find("\n---\n")?;
670	    let rest = &after_fm[close + 5..];
671	    let (before_delta, _) = rest.split_once("## Handoff Delta")?;
672	    let body: Vec<&str> = before_delta
673	        .lines()
674	        .map(|l| l.trim())
675	        .filter(|l| !l.is_empty() && !l.starts_with('#'))

677	    Some(body.join("\n"))

680	/// sha256 of a byte string — the handoff's `source-sha` preimage (the subagent's raw findings), so
681	/// a governed handoff is verifiably derived from those exact findings. Shells out (same tool-fallback
682	/// order as `verify-closeout.sh#_sha256`) rather than add a crate for one hash; this codebase already
683	/// shells to git/sha tools throughout.
684	pub fn sha256_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {
685	    let variants: [(&str, &[&str]); 2] = [("sha256sum", &[]), ("shasum", &["-a", "256"])];
686	    for (cmd, args) in variants {
687	        let mut child = match Command::new(cmd)
688	            .args(args)
689	            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
690	            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
691	            .stderr(Stdio::null())
692	            .spawn()
693	        {
694	            Ok(c) => c,
695	            Err(_) => continue,
696	        };
697	        if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {
698	            if stdin.write_all(bytes).is_err() {
699	                continue;
700	            }
701	        }
702	        if let Ok(out) = child.wait_with_output() {
703	            if out.status.success() {
704	                if let Some(h) = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout)
705	                    .split_whitespace()
706	                    .next()
707	                {
708	                    return Some(h.to_string());
709	                }
710	            }
711	        }
712	    }
713	    None
714	}

783	/// Parse handoff TEXT into a `Handoff` (pure — the testable core). `session`/`path` come from where
784	/// it was found rather than from the frontmatter: the path is the placement SoT, and trusting a
785	/// self-declared `session:` would let a misfiled handoff claim any session it liked.
786	pub fn parse_handoff(text: &str, session: u32, path: &str) -> Result<Handoff, String> {
787	    validate_handoff(text)?;
788	    let body = handoff_body(text).ok_or_else(|| "handoff has no findings body".to_string())?;
789	    // Every displayed field must come from the FRONTMATTER BLOCK, not merely from somewhere in the
790	    // file. `validate_handoff` accepts a `role:` line anywhere (it scans all lines), so without this
791	    // a file whose keys sit in the body would parse into a `Handoff` with blank fields and render as
792	    // "  (agent: , captured: )" — a broken artifact reading as a good one. Fail closed instead.
793	    let field = |key: &str| {
794	        frontmatter_value(text, key)
795	            .ok_or_else(|| format!("handoff frontmatter block has no `{key}` value"))
796	    };
797	    Ok(Handoff {
798	        role: field("role:")?,
799	        session,
800	        path: path.to_string(),
801	        agent: field("agent:")?,
802	        captured: field("captured:")?,
803	        source_sha: field("source-sha:")?,

808	/// The value of a frontmatter `key:` line, trimmed. Only the frontmatter block is searched (the
809	/// text before the closing `---` fence), so a body line that merely starts with `agent:` cannot
810	/// impersonate a frontmatter field.
811	fn frontmatter_value(text: &str, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
812	    let after_fm = text.strip_prefix("---\n")?;
813	    let close = after_fm.find("\n---\n")?;
814	    after_fm[..close]
815	        .lines()
816	        .find_map(|l| l.trim_start().strip_prefix(key))
817	        .map(|v| v.trim().to_string())
818	        .filter(|v| !v.is_empty())
819	}

821	/// Read one role's governed handoff for `session` back off disk (the module's one narrow read
822	/// edge — fs-read-only, no writes, no processes; testable against a tempdir). An unreadable file
823	/// is reported as `Malformed`, never silently `Absent`.
824	pub fn read_handoff(root: &std::path::Path, role: &Role, session: u32) -> HandoffRead {
825	    let rel = role.handoff_rel(session);
826	    let path = root.join(&rel);
827	    if !path.exists() {
828	        return HandoffRead::Absent;
829	    }
830	    match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
831	        Err(e) => HandoffRead::Malformed(rel, format!("unreadable: {e}")),
832	        Ok(text) => match parse_handoff(&text, session, &rel) {
833	            Ok(h) => HandoffRead::Found(h),
834	            Err(reason) => HandoffRead::Malformed(rel, reason),
835	        },
836	    }
837	}

839	/// Every registered role's handoff for `session`, dropping the `Absent` ones. Empty vec = this
840	/// session simply had no fleet work, which every caller must treat as normal and silent.
841	pub fn read_handoffs(root: &std::path::Path, session: u32) -> Vec<HandoffRead> {
842	    ROLES
843	        .iter()
844	        .map(|r| read_handoff(root, r, session))
845	        .filter(|h| !matches!(h, HandoffRead::Absent))
846	        .collect()
847	}

849	/// Render read handoffs as the block a consuming station prints: who produced it, when, where it
850	/// lives, and the first `head` findings lines INLINE (a path alone is not consumption). Empty
851	/// input renders the empty string — absence prints nothing at all.
852	pub fn format_handoff_brief(reads: &[HandoffRead], head: usize) -> String {
853	    let mut s = String::new();
854	    for r in reads {
855	        match r {
856	            HandoffRead::Absent => {}
857	            HandoffRead::Malformed(path, reason) => {
858	                s.push_str(&format!(
859	                    "  ⚠ {path} exists but does not satisfy the handoff contract ({reason}) \
860	                     — not used\n"
861	                ));
862	            }
863	            HandoffRead::Found(h) => {
864	                s.push_str(&format!(
865	                    "  {role} (agent: {agent}, captured: {captured})\n    {path}\n",
866	                    role = h.role,
867	                    agent = h.agent,
868	                    captured = h.captured,
869	                    path = h.path,
870	                ));
871	                for line in h.head_lines(head) {
872	                    let clipped: String = line.chars().take(110).collect();
873	                    let ell = if line.chars().count() > 110 {
874	                        "…"
875	                    } else {
876	                        ""
877	                    };
878	                    s.push_str(&format!("    · {clipped}{ell}\n"));
879	                }
880	                // Never let a truncated head read as the whole brief — say how much was left out
881	                // and where the rest is. A partial view that looks complete is a false green.
882	                let omitted = h.omitted_lines(head);
883	                if omitted > 0 {
884	                    s.push_str(&format!(
885	                        "    · … {omitted} more line(s) — full findings at {}\n",
886	                        h.path
887	                    ));
888	                }
889	            }
890	        }
891	    }
892	    s
893	}
